data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the same 3 files (.SRCINFO, .gitignore, PKGBUILD). The deepseek model correctly identified the package as safe: standard Go build with pinned GitHub source, valid SHA-256 checksum, no command substitution in global scope, no obfuscated code or suspicious network requests. The qwen3-235b model's 'inconclusive' result was caused solely by an API error (HTTP 400) when reviewing .gitignore, not a security concern. The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR practices for Go packages with proper integrity verification.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement (inconclusive vs safe) was caused by a tool error in the qwen3-235b model, which failed to review .gitignore due to an HTTP 400 API error. This is an infrastructure failure, not a security finding. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b model failed to review .gitignore due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in the final verdict. An API error on a non-executable file like .gitignore should not force an 'inconclusive' verdict when all other files are safe.
The audit system should implement retry logic or fallback handling for transient API errors to prevent tool failures from affecting security verdicts.
When a model encounters an API error on a file, the system should note it as a coverage issue but not let it override clear safety findings from other files.
